title: Long-tail Quantization Bench and Regression Sentinel for Runtime Profiles
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We need an operational benchmarking harness that measures quality/perf trade-offs across FP16/INT8/INT4 profiles under realistic, long-tail workloads and reliably detects regressions during model or kernel changes. Existing quant benches focus on mean throughput or focused workloads and miss long-tail patterns, mixed-batching effects, and subtle quality regressions that only appear under prefix-heavy or streaming traffic.

Goal: Build a repeatable, CI-integrated 'Long-tail Quant Bench' and a lightweight 'Regression Sentinel' that continuously runs critical profile comparisons and emits deterministic pass/fail signals for runtime changes. The harness must report: tokens_per_sec (steady-state), p50/p95/p99 latencies, KV-cache hit-adjusted throughput, memory footprint, and quality delta measured by embedding cosine similarity and token-level divergence on evaluation prompt sets.

Scope:
- Benchmark target profiles: FP16 baseline, INT8 (per-channel symmetric), INT8 (per-tensor asymmetric), INT4 mixed-precision (KV only / activations only), and fallback FP16-quant fallback chains.
- Workloads: short-chat (<=128 tokens), long-context (>=4096 tokens with KV cache re-use), streaming/partial-output latencies, and mixed-concurrency traces (1-64 concurrent streams) sampled from production traffic fingerprints.
- Metrics: tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, 95th-percentile CPU/GPU utilization, memory high-water mark, quality delta (embedding cosine, top-k token overlap, logit gap on answer tokens), and regression score (composite).
- Regression detection: automated statistical checks comparing new runs to baseline with configurable thresholds and lookback. Support both absolute thresholds and relative delta with FDR control to avoid noisy alerts.

Deliverables:
1) Harness code (pytest-compatible harness + runner) that can run locally, in CI, and on dedicated infra.
2) Baseline profile snapshots for a selected family of models and representative datasets.
3) A lightweight sentinel job that runs nightly against latest runtime and posts results to Slack/Datadog + creates Linear regression issue for failing gates.
4) Documentation and runbook describing how to add new profiles and interpret signals.

Non-goals: full fuzz testing of kernels, exhaustive model family coverage across all architectures (start with 2 model families).
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run a defined profile matrix (3 models x 4 quant profiles x 4 workload types) and produce JSON metrics within 2 hours
Sentinel nightly job executes in CI and posts summarized regression results to #bench-alerts Slack channel
Regression detector creates a Linear ticket when composite regression score exceeds configured threshold and includes links to diffs, golden prompts, and sample outputs
Bench results include stable quality metrics (embedding cosine and token overlap) computed reproducibly and stored in blob storage with versioned keys
Runbook published in Confluence describing how to onboard a new model and how to interpret p95 vs tokens/sec trade-offs

notes: Trade-offs discussed: tighter quality thresholds reduce cost savings from INT4; for latency-sensitive routes we will prefer INT8-per-channel with KV-cache preservation. Decision: allow INT4 for low-risk routes with canary gating.
Edge cases: streaming token-level latency regressions can be masked by aggregated tokens/sec. Sentinel must track both incremental per-token latency and aggregate throughput.
Operational: include CPU/GPU percent time-in-kernel metric to detect kernel thrashing and queueing effects that correlate with p95 spikes.
